title: Partner contract negotiation scratchpad
content:
Context: personal scratchpad for upcoming negotiation call with Acme Analytics (potential OEM partner). This is messy — notes to self, quick fallback language, red flags, and negotiation scripts. Keep short bulleted points for call prep.

SUMMARY PRIORITIES (ranked):
- Protect Redwood from unlimited downstream liability and long-tail IP claims. prioritize: Liability cap, indemnity carveouts, insurance.
- Keep customer data processing bounded: no broad audit rights, limit data export, require pseudonymization where feasible.
- Preserve Redwood ownership of models/derivatives; limit partner rights to use outputs only for agreed integration. Avoid joint ownership language.
- SLA credits over termination triggers; avoid termination for convenience on our side that leaves us exposed.

QUICK RED FLAGS TO SPOT IN THEIR DRAFT:
- Unlimited indemnity or mutual indemnity that includes indirect/third-party claims (push for narrow scope).
- Broad IP assignment or ownership of "derivatives" without definition (ask for examples).
- Right to copy or host our model weights or internal data sets.
- Unfettered audit rights and on-site inspections.
- Auto-renewal + punitive termination notice and retrofit obligations.
- Broad export-control or sanctions termination that could be used opportunistically.

CLAUSE-BY-CLAUSE PLAY:
1) Liability / Cap
- Suggest: cap = greater of (6 months fees paid under agreement, $1M) — good starting point.
- Push back on unlimited or very large caps. If they insist on higher cap, trade for higher insurance limits and narrower indemnity scope.
- Proposal language snippet: "Aggregate liability shall be limited to the amount paid by Partner to Redwood under this Agreement in the 12 months preceding the claim, or $1,000,000, whichever is greater."

2) Indemnity
- Our ask: narrow to IP infringement claims and gross negligence/willful misconduct on their side. We will indemnify for third-party claims that arise from Redwood-delivered software IP, with standard notice/cooperation procedures.
- Push: mutual indemnity only for third-party IP claims; no indemnity for regulatory fines or diminution of business.

3) IP and Rights to Outputs
- We must retain model, training data, architecture, and improvements. Partner gets a restricted, non-exclusive license to use API outputs for integration described in SOW. No rights to rehost, retrain, or create derivative models.
- If they request derivative rights for feature engineering, require a separate commercial arrangement and strong attribution clauses.

4) Data / Security / Privacy
- Data use: Redwood processes partner-provided data for the purpose of delivering services, with retention limits (default: 90 days unless SLA/paid retention agreed).
- Push back on any clause that allows them to demand raw data exports without formal legal process.
- Security incidents: require 72-hour notification for incidents affecting partner data; Redwood to provide remediation plan and timeline.

5) Audit Rights
- Limit to annual remote audits, or records access upon reasonable notice and for narrow purpose (security/compliance only). No broad on-site hacking or surprise audits.

6) Termination & Transition
- Avoid short termination-for-convenience windows that leave us with unrecoverable costs. If partner wants termination for convenience, require 60 days notice plus payment for committed reserved capacity.
- Transition assistance: limited to 90 days at standard rates, unless extended transition bundled in SOW.

7) SLA / Availability
- Prefer credits, not termination, for sporadic outages. Reserve termination only for sustained SLA breaches (3 consecutive months below target).
- Define measurement windows and acceptance tests in SOW to avoid ambiguous rollback triggers.

8) Compliance & Export Control
- Add language that neither party will be required to violate applicable export controls; allow for termination if compliance demands make performance illegal.

NEGOTIATION SCRIPTS / TL;DR LINES (for quick use on calls):
- If they ask for higher liability: "We can consider a higher cap in exchange for a reciprocal reduction in indemnity scope and higher insurance coverage — let's quantify the delta."
- If they push IP assignment: "We need to keep core IP and model ownership — we can license outputs and provide a usage right tied to the integration in the SOW."
- On audits: "Remote, scoped audits are fine. For on-site, let's scope and pre-approve logistics and frequency."

FALLBACK POSITIONS (if they push hard):
- Move from $1M cap to $3M if they accept clarified indemnity carveouts and agree to 2x insurance premium coverage.
- If partner demands derivative rights, require a revenue share and strict use-case limitations + escrow of model weights only under strict conditions.

NOTES TO SELF / OPEN QUESTIONS TO RAISE WITH LEGAL TEAM:
- Confirm default data retention policy (90 days) aligns with SOC2/KMS policies. Ticket: JIRA-4170 (data-retention).
- Are we comfortable with 72-hour breach notification? Legal suggested 48 hours — check current infra detection SLA.
- Clarify language for "derivative" — ask legal to draft a short definition with examples.

WORKFLOW / ACTION ITEMS BEFORE CALL:
- Pull latest MSA template from contracts repo (see linked PR).
- Ask infra: can we guarantee 99.5% for next quarter on dedicated pool? If no, set expectation to 99%.
- Draft counter clause snippets and send to Jordan / Priya for quick review (turnaround: 24h).

REFERENCE LANGUAGE (quick cut-and-paste candidates):
- Liability cap snippet (see above).
- Data retention: "Redwood will retain Partner Data for no longer than 90 days following processing, except to the extent required by law or as otherwise agreed in writing."
- Audit: "Partner may conduct one remote audit per 12-month period with at least 30 days' prior notice; on-site audits require mutual agreement and reimbursement for Redwood's reasonable costs."

FINAL: keep this as a working doc. Expect to prune and move sanitized clauses into contracts repo after internal review. Mark items we want Legal to redline in the canonical MSA.
